title: Generic bounded constructibility for an open immersion
statement:
Let $S$ be integral and of finite type over a field $k$, let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, and let
$j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$S$-schemes. For a constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf $F$
on $X$, there is a nonempty open $U\subset S$ such that
$Rj_{U,*}F|_{X_U}$ belongs to $D^b_c(Y_U,\mathbf F_\ell)$
and, for every morphism $T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$, its canonical base-change morphism

$$
Rj_{U,*}F|_{X_U}\big|_{Y_T}
\longrightarrow Rj_{T,*}F|_{X_T}
$$

is an isomorphism.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories.

proof.text:
Preliminaries used throughout. Shrink the integral base to a nonempty affine open. All finite-type schemes in the argument are Noetherian: apply [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] on a finite affine cover and glue the descending-chain property. Thus they have finitely many irreducible components, and all further base changes in the assertion have Noetherian source. Pullback for the constant ring $\mathbf F_\ell$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The canonical comparison and its invertibility can be checked after forgetting coefficients by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]; this permits use of the abelian-sheaf exchange formulas below without identifying coefficient categories.
The assertion is local for a finite open cover of the target. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction] identifies underived direct image restricted to a target open with direct image of the source restriction. A bounded-below injective resolution restricts to an injective resolution by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], giving the same identification for derived direct image and its actual exchange map. Vanishing and invertibility are checked on the cover. Constructible stratifications on its finitely many members give a finite global stratification: order the members and subtract the preceding members from each stratum. Take the union of their finite cohomological intervals. Thus finitely many good base opens can be intersected, and we may work on affine target charts whenever needed.

We prove both assertions together by induction on $n=\dim X_{k(S)}$, with the empty generic source as the initial case. At every stage the result for open immersions also gives the result for quasi-compact immersions with the same source dimension: factor such an immersion as an open immersion followed by a closed immersion using [lem-pqf-qc-immersion-open-closed-factor], and use exact constructibility-preserving closed direct image [lem-fin-closed-immersion], finite exchange [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange], and the derived composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. The exchange for the composite is the pasting formula [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting], read after forgetting coefficients as in step 1.
For the open immersion at hand replace $Y$ by the closure of $X$ with its scheme-theoretic structure, using [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] for the quasi-compact immersion $j$. This gives a dense open factor and a closed inclusion into the original target: on an affine chart its ideal consists of sections whose restriction to $X$ is zero, so it restricts to the zero ideal on $X$ and $X$ remains open. Its underlying space is the topological closure, so $X$ is dense there. The preceding closed-image argument transfers the conclusion back. Remove the closures in $S$ of the images of those finitely many irreducible components not dominating $S$. If the generic source is empty, what remains is empty. If $n=0$, each component of the generic target meets the dense generic source and is zero-dimensional. The generic target is discrete by [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete]; its dense open therefore contains every point. The complement $C=Y\setminus X$ therefore has empty generic fibre. Cover $C$ by finitely many affine charts over the affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$. For each coordinate ring $B$, $B\otimes_A\operatorname{Frac}(A)=0$, so some nonzero $a_B\in A$ kills $1_B$. Invert their product. Then $C$ is empty and $j$ is the identity, which proves the base case. Assume henceforth the simultaneous assertion for source generic dimension at most $n-1$, allowing any integral finite-type base over $k$.

First construct a good open with finite complement when $b:Y\to S$ is projective and $X$ is dense. Cover $Y$ by finitely many affine opens $Y_\alpha$ and choose closed embeddings $Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{m_\alpha}_S$, with $m_\alpha\geq1$ (append a zero coordinate if necessary). For each coordinate $t_{\alpha r}$, regard $X\cap Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y_\alpha$ as an open immersion over the integral base $\mathbf A^1_S$. By [lem-fin-coordinate-generic-dimension] its generic source dimension is at most $n-1$, possibly empty. Induction gives a dense open $V_{\alpha r}\subset\mathbf A^1_S$ over whose preimage both assertions hold. These assertions include every induced base change from a Noetherian $T\to S$: the open inverse image of $V_{\alpha r}$ in $\mathbf A^1_T$ is Noetherian and maps to $V_{\alpha r}$. By step 1 the union $G$ of the finitely many good target opens has bounded constructible direct image with a common finite cohomological range and the canonical exchange is invertible on $G_T$. Apply [lem-fin-projective-coordinate-boundary] to shrink $S$ so that the reduced closed complement $Z=Y\setminus G$ is finite over $S$.

Prove the dimension-$n$ assertion first when $X\to S$ is smooth and $F$ finite locally constant. By step 1 work on one affine chart of $Y$. A finite generating set of its coordinate algebra gives a closed embedding in $\mathbf A^m_S$. Apply [lem-chow-closed-model] to its quasi-compact immersion into $\mathbf P^m_S$ to take the closure there: equivalently homogenize the defining ideal and saturate by the distinguished homogeneous coordinate. On the chart where that coordinate is invertible the ideal dehomogenizes to the original ideal, so the original affine target is open in this projective scheme. The original $X$ is still open. Take its closure there as in step 2, using [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image]. This gives a projective target to which step 3 applies; it is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], and restriction later recovers the original chart. In particular the smooth source morphism $a=bj$ is now separated, since $X$ is open in a projective $S$-scheme, and is of finite type.
Put $K=Rj_*F\in D^+(Y,\mathbf F_\ell)$. Step 3 gives $K|_G\in D^b_c(G)$. By [lem-asd-smooth-generic-direct-image], after shrinking once more, $Ra_*F$ is bounded with finite locally constant cohomology. The composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies this with $Rb_*K$. All hypotheses of [lem-fin-finite-boundary-reconstruction] now hold: $b$ is proper between finite-type schemes, $Z\to S$ is finite, and the two required restrictions/direct images are bounded constructible. It follows that $K\in D^b_c(Y)$.

For any Noetherian $T\to S$, let $c:g_Y^*K\to Rj_{T,*}g_X^*F$ be the canonical exchange. It is an isomorphism on $G_T$ by step 3. Proper base change [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] applied to the torsion underlying complex of $K$ gives $g^*Rb_*K\simeq Rb_{T,*}g_Y^*K$. Under the direct-image composition comparisons, part (3), vertical pasting, of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting] says that the exchange for $a=bj$ equals proper exchange for $b$ followed by $Rb_{T,*}c$. The former exchange for $a$ is invertible by [lem-asd-smooth-generic-direct-image]. Therefore $Rb_{T,*}c$ is invertible. These are the actual morphisms after forgetting coefficients, and [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] reflects invertibility for $\mathbf F_\ell$-complexes. Properness of $b_T$ follows from [lem-kun-proper-stability], and finiteness of $Z_T\to T$ follows by tensoring a finite algebra presentation. Apply [lem-fin-finite-boundary-comparison] over $T$ to conclude that $c$ is invertible. Both arguments of $c$ are bounded below; no constructibility of its target was assumed. This completes the smooth locally constant case at dimension at most $n$.

For general $F$, invoke [lem-fin-generic-radicial-smoothing] after removing vertical components as in step 2: shrink $S$ and take a finite radicial surjection $S'\to S$ with a dense smooth open $v:V\hookrightarrow (X_{S'})_{\mathrm{red}}$ on which the pulled-back $F$ is finite locally constant. We may replace $S'$ by its reduction: finite radicial surjectivity is preserved, its underlying space is the irreducible space of $S$, hence it is integral; smoothness of $V$ persists by base change. Replace $X_{S'}$ and $Y_{S'}$ by reductions too. Reductions are surjective closed immersions, hence universal homeomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism]. A finite radicial surjection is a closed bijection by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] and the definition of radicial; this justifies the irreducibility assertion above. Thus the reductions and all their base changes are universal homeomorphisms, so [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] gives equivalences preserving pullbacks, direct images and cohomology. The canonical exchange is preserved because it is the adjunction-mate composite defining [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Constructibility is unchanged, using the same topological strata and their finite locally constant sheaves.
Work now over this integral base. The smooth-source case already proved at dimension at most $n$ applies to $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ and $jv:V\hookrightarrow Y$. Intersect their two nonempty good base opens. Choose the cone triangle of the adjunction unit $F\to Rv_*v^*F$, denoting its third vertex by $\Delta$. The first two vertices are bounded constructible, and the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], together with closure under kernels, cokernels and extensions [thm-constructible-serre], makes $\Delta$ bounded constructible. Restricting to $V$ makes the unit the identity, so $v^*\Delta=0$. The triangle of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] for the reduced complement $i:W\hookrightarrow X$ therefore gives the canonical isomorphism $\Delta\simeq i_*i^*\Delta$. This uses the ordinary finite-coefficient etale localization theorem, not a definition of extension by zero or a pro-etale analogue.

By the dimension assertion in [lem-fin-generic-radicial-smoothing], the complement $W$ has generic dimension at most $n-1$. Pullback $i^*$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and preserves constructibility: pull back the finitely many constructible strata of $\Delta$ and their locally constant restrictions. Thus $Q=i^*\Delta$ has finitely many nonzero constructible cohomology sheaves. Apply lower-dimensional induction, extended to immersions in step 2, to $ji:W\to Y$ and each such sheaf. Intersect the finitely many resulting base opens.
The truncation triangles [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] give a finite filtration of $Q$ with successive vertices $\mathcal H^q(Q)[-q]$: if its cohomology is supported in $[a,b]$, begin at $\tau_{\le a-1}Q=0$ and add one cohomology sheaf through degree $b$. Applying the triangulated direct image [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] preserves these triangles. The long exact sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] and [thm-constructible-serre] prove bounded constructibility by finite induction (take a finite union of degree bounds). The exchange morphisms commute with shifts and form morphisms of triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated]; the cohomology long exact sequences then show inductively that their third components are isomorphisms when the first two are, degree by degree. This checks the actual exchange for $Q$, not just separate existence of endpoint isomorphisms. These abelian exchange assertions apply to modules by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. The direct-image composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies $R(ji)_*Q$ with $Rj_*\Delta$; closed exchange [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] and vertical pasting [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting] give the corresponding exchange identification.
Apply $Rj_*$ to $F\to Rv_*v^*F\to\Delta\to F[1]$. The middle vertex is $R(jv)_*v^*F$ and the third is the just-treated $Rj_*\Delta$. The same long exact sequence proves bounded constructibility of $Rj_*F$. Under base change the triangle for $v$ identifies with the corresponding triangle for $v_T$, because its unit commutes with pullback and the exchange for $v$ is invertible. The exchange for $j$ gives a morphism of these triangles, with invertible middle component by the smooth case for $jv$ and invertible third component by the preceding finite filtration. The long exact sequences imply that the first component, the desired exchange for $F$, is invertible.

It remains to descend from the good open $U'\subset S'$ of steps 6--7. A finite radicial surjection is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces: it is bijective by surjectivity and universal injectivity, and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Consequently $S'\setminus U'$ has closed image $C$ in the original shrunken base, and $C$ misses the generic point since $U'$ is nonempty in the irreducible space $S'$. For the nonempty open $U=S\setminus C$, its full preimage $S'_U$ lies inside $U'$. Over $S'_U$ bounded constructibility and compatibility with every further Noetherian base change have been proved, including the reduction identifications of step 6. Apply [lem-fin-radicial-exchange-descent] to the finite radicial surjection $S'_U\to U$. It gives both assertions on $U$, completing the induction. This last topological argument also covers zero-dimensional bases; it does not use a dimension estimate for a closed subset.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $S$ be integral and of finite type over a field $k$, let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, and let
$j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$S$-schemes. For a constructible $\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf $F$
on $X$, there is a nonempty open $U\subset S$ such that
$Rj_{U,*}F|_{X_U}$ belongs to $D^b_c(Y_U,\mathbf F_\ell)$
and, for every morphism $T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$, its canonical base-change morphism

$$
Rj_{U,*}F|_{X_U}\big|_{Y_T}
\longrightarrow Rj_{T,*}F|_{X_T}
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Throughout this proof all base changes have Noetherian source.
We prove the two assertions simultaneously, so that every use of
the induction includes the specific exchange map. Replace $Y$
by the scheme-theoretic closure of $X$; the original immersion
is its composite with a closed immersion. Closed direct image
is exact and preserves constructibility by
[lem-fin-closed-immersion], and it commutes with base change by
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange]. We may therefore assume
that $X$ is dense in $Y$. The same observation extends any
case already proved for a dense open immersion to an arbitrary
immersion with that bound on the generic dimension of its source.

Induct on $n=\dim X_{k(S)}$. Before starting, remove the
closures of the images of the finitely many irreducible components
of $Y$ that do not dominate $S$. For an empty generic fiber
the remaining scheme is empty. For $n=0$, the dense open
$X_{k(S)}$ contains every point of the zero-dimensional
Noetherian space $Y_{k(S)}$, so it equals that space.
The closed complement $Y\setminus X$ has empty generic fiber.
Its finite affine presentations show that it becomes empty after
inverting one nonzero element of the base: over the fraction
field each coordinate ring is zero, so a nonzero base element
kills its unit; use the product for a finite affine cover.
Thus, after shrinking, $j$ is the identity and the assertion
holds. Assume now the assertion for generic source dimension
at most $n-1$, including all immersions as above.

*First step: the good locus has finite complement.*
The question is local on $Y$, and $Y$ has a finite affine
cover. For this step suppose $Y$ projective over an affine
open of $S$, and cover it by finitely many affine schemes
$Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{m_\alpha}_S$.
For each coordinate, regard
$X\cap Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y_\alpha$ as an immersion
over the integral finite-type base $\mathbf A^1_S$.
Its generic source dimension is at most $n-1$ by
[lem-fin-coordinate-generic-dimension]. The induction
hypothesis supplies a dense open $V_{\alpha r}\subset\mathbf A^1_S$
over whose inverse image the direct image is bounded constructible
and commutes with all base changes. This includes every base
change induced from $T\to S$: restrict the induced morphism
$\mathbf A^1_T\to\mathbf A^1_S$ to $V_{\alpha r}$.
There are finitely many coordinate pairs. Their union $G$
therefore has both properties, with a common finite cohomological
range. By [lem-fin-projective-coordinate-boundary], shrink
$S$ so that $Z=Y\setminus G$, with reduced structure, is
finite over $S$.

*Second step: smooth source and locally constant sheaf.*
Assume $X\to S$ is smooth and $F$ locally constant.
The assertion can be checked on each member of a finite affine
cover of $Y$. For one such member, embed it in affine space
and take its projective closure. The original affine member
is open in this closure, so $X$ remains an open subscheme of
the projective closure. Replacing the closure by the closure of
$X$ makes $X$ dense. This operation changes no generic
dimension of $X$, and the desired result on the projective
closure restricts to the original member.
We can thus use the first step with $b:Y\to S$ projective.
Set $K=Rj_*F$ and $a=bj:X\to S$. The first step proves
$K|_G\in D^b_c(G)$. After one further shrinking,
[lem-asd-smooth-generic-direct-image] proves
$Ra_*F=Rb_*K\in D^b_c(S)$.
[lem-fin-finite-boundary-reconstruction] now gives
$K\in D^b_c(Y)$.

For any $T\to S$ with Noetherian $T$, let $c:K|_{Y_T}\to Rj_{T,*}F|_{X_T}$
be its exchange morphism. On $G_T$ it is an isomorphism by
the first step. After applying $Rb_{T,*}$, proper base change
[thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] and the composition rule
[sbc-lem-base-change-composition] identify the resulting
morphism with the exchange for $a$, which is an isomorphism
by the smooth-source lemma. The base change of $Z\to S$
is finite. Hence [lem-fin-finite-boundary-comparison],
applied over $T$, says that $c$ is an isomorphism.
Notice that the target of $c$ need only start in $D^+$;
its boundedness follows from the proved isomorphism.
This proves the entire dimension-$n$ assertion whenever the
source is smooth and the coefficient sheaf is locally constant.

*Third step: arbitrary constructible sheaf.*
By [lem-fin-generic-radicial-smoothing], after shrinking and
making a finite radicial surjective base change, the reduction of
$X$ has a dense smooth open $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ on which
$F$ is locally constant. Replacing the schemes by their
reductions does not change their etale topoi, by
[thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance].
The second step, which has already been proved at dimension
$n$, applies both to $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ and to
$jv:V\hookrightarrow Y$. After intersecting the two resulting
base opens, their derived direct images are bounded constructible
and commute with every base change. Form the triangle

$$
F\longrightarrow Rv_*v^*F\longrightarrow\Delta\longrightarrow F[1].
\tag{1}
$$

The first arrow is the adjunction unit. Both first terms are
bounded constructible, so the cohomology long exact sequence and
[thm-constructible-serre] show that $\Delta$ is
bounded constructible. The unit is the identity after restriction
to $V$, hence $\Delta|_V=0$. For the reduced closed complement
$i:W\hookrightarrow X$, termwise open–closed localization from
[def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] identifies
$\Delta=i_*i^*\Delta$. The generic dimension of $W$ is less
than $n$.

Apply the induction hypothesis to the immersion $ji:W\to Y$
and to each of the finitely many constructible sheaves
$\mathcal H^q(i^*\Delta)$. Intersect the finitely many base
opens. Finite truncation triangles, or their bounded spectral
sequence [thm-sp-truncation-e2], prove that
$R(ji)_*i^*\Delta=Rj_*\Delta$ is bounded constructible and
commutes with every base change. Only a finite number of
cohomology sheaves and a bounded truncation filtration occur.
Apply $Rj_*$ to (1). The middle term is
$R(jv)_*v^*F$, already handled by the second step, and the
third term has just been handled by lower-dimensional induction.
The long exact sequence proves bounded constructibility of
$Rj_*F$. After any base change, the second-step exchange
identifies the pullback of (1) with the analogous triangle for
$v_T$. The three exchange morphisms consequently form a
morphism of triangles; the second and third are isomorphisms,
so the first is an isomorphism as well.
Finally [lem-fin-radicial-exchange-descent] descends the result
through the finite radicial base change. Its hypothesis must be checked
over the whole base to which it is applied, so we first produce an open of
$S$ whose preimage lies inside the good open. Let $U\subseteq S$ be
the open over which the preceding steps hold and let
$U'\subseteq S'_{U}=S'\times_SU$ be the nonempty open of $S'_{U}$ on
which they were verified. Since $S'\to S$ is finite, surjective and
radicial, it is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces; $S$ being
integral, $S'$ and $S'_{U}$ are therefore irreducible of dimension
$\dim S$. The complement $F=S'_{U}\setminus U'$ is closed in
$S'_{U}$, and its image $C\subseteq U$ is closed because
$S'_{U}\to U$ is finite. If $C=U$, then $F\to U$ is surjective, so
$\dim F\ge\dim U=\dim S'_{U}$, which is impossible for a proper closed
subset of the irreducible $S'_{U}$. Hence $C\neq U$, and for the
nonempty open $U_1=U\setminus C$ the preimage $S'_{U_1}$ is contained
in $U'$. Applying [lem-fin-radicial-exchange-descent] over
$U_1$, and intersecting with the finitely many opens already produced,
completes the induction.
